Frequently Asked Questions
Commonly asked questions about Wasalt and the services we provide
What is Wasalt?
Wasalt is a leading platform in Saudi Arabia for electronic real estate services, licensed by the Real Estate General Authority (REGA).
How can I list my property on Wasalt?
To list your property on Wasalt, start by creating an account, then entering property details, uploading photos, and setting prices, primarily through the Wasalt App, Wasalt Business App, or website.
How do I log into my Wasalt account
Click the profile icon (top left on the web or via the burger menu in the app). Enter your mobile number and complete OTP verification.
What is Wasalt Auctions?
Wasalt Auctions is a feature where real estate assets are sold through timed auctions. Bidders can compete to determine the final sale price. Auctions include assets from private sellers and those in collaboration with Infath (Entrustment and Liquidation Center).
What is Matchmaker, and how does it work?
Matchmaker helps you find potential leads based on your live listings. It matches leads based on the property type, purpose, district, and category of your live property. Once your listing is live, Matchmaker will show leads that match those preferences, making it easier for you to connect with the right leads.
What real estate services does Wasalt offer?
Wasalt is an AI-powered real estate portal for verified properties, projects, masterplans, online auctions, and daily rentals. Providing an enhanced search experience for users pursuing their ideal homes.

Riyadh offers rental options for all needs, from modern apartments in Al Olaya to spacious villas in Al Nakheel. The city caters to families, professionals, and expatriates with diverse choices, whether they need an apartment, villa, or a furnished apartment.
What is the rental price in Riyadh on average?
Rental prices in Riyadh vary by location and property type. Studio apartments start at SAR 20,000 annually, while one- and two-bedroom units range from SAR 30,000 to SAR 100,000. Standalone villas begin at SAR 80,000, with compound villas reaching SAR 300,000 in areas like the Diplomatic Quarter. Furnished apartments start at SAR 5,000 monthly, while luxury serviced units in KAFD can exceed SAR 150,000 annually.
What Are the Requirements for Expats to Rent a Property in Riyadh?
Expatriates renting in Riyadh need a valid Iqama (residence permit) and proof of income, often through an employment contract. A security deposit (one to three months' rent) is required, and rental payments are usually made yearly or semi-annually. Contracts must be registered through Ejar, a government platform that ensures tenant rights. Some landlords may request additional documents, like sponsorship details, especially for compound rentals.
How Can I Find Rental Units in Riyadh?
Finding a rental property in Riyadh involves online research, real estate agents, and personal visits. Platform like Wasalt Saudi list apartments, villas, and compounds with search filters. Expats often rely on forums like Expat.com and Facebook groups for recommendations. With multiple resources available, finding the right home in Riyadh is more accessible than ever.
What Should I Consider When Choosing a Rental Property in Riyadh?
Choosing the right rental in Riyadh depends on location, budget, and lifestyle needs. Business professionals prefer areas like Al Olaya, while families opt for Al Yasmin. Compare rental prices and payment terms, considering hidden costs. Expats often choose compounds for security and amenities, while standalone villas offer more privacy. Ensure the lease is registered with Ejar for legal protection and verify the landlord’s credibility. If needed, prioritize safety, access to services, and proximity to schools.
